messages:
acme-sre: Hey team — after the cert rotation last night some of our VPC clients are intermittently failing TLS with `x509: certificate signed by unknown authority`. Failures only hit ~20% of requests and seem tied to specific IPs behind our DNS. Not sure where to start, attaching minimal repro: 

acme-sre: curl output (fails):
```
* Connected to api.customer.internal (10.10.4.23) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake error: 1408F10B:SSL routines:ssl3_get_client_certificate:peer did not return a certificate
* Closing connection 0
curl: (35) TLS handshake error
```

acme-sre: openssl check to same IP shows only leaf cert returned:
```
$ openssl s_client -connect 10.10.4.23:443 -servername api.customer.internal -showcerts
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=0 CN = api.customer.internal
verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate
---
# only one certificate block (leaf) printed
---
```

maria: thanks — can you also run `openssl s_client -connect api.customer.internal:443 -showcerts -servername api.customer.internal` (no IP) and `dig +short api.customer.internal A` and paste results? we want to see if the IPs differ and whether any endpoint serves a fullchain vs leaf-only.

acme-sre: ran both, results below. DNS returns 3 IPs (10.10.4.21, 10.10.4.22, 10.10.4.23). Connecting to .21 and .22 shows fullchain, .23 shows only leaf. `dig` output:
```
$ dig +short api.customer.internal
10.10.4.21
10.10.4.22
10.10.4.23
```

acme-sre: openssl to .21 prints leaf+intermediate chain; .23 prints only leaf (same as earlier).

alex: weird — our rotator upload logs show the full bundle was pushed to all edges. ops-bot can you pull rotator artifact checksums for the deploy that ran at 02:12 UTC?

ops-bot: rotator: uploaded cert bundle id=rb-20260317-0212 sha256=8f3a... to edge-proxy-1,edge-proxy-2,edge-proxy-3 at 2026-03-17T02:12:43Z. upload_status=ok

alex: so the bundle was uploaded. next guess: one of the edge proxies is serving a different nginx/HAProxy config (maybe missing `fullchain` directive). ryan, can you check config drift for edge-proxy-3 and last deploy logs?

ryan: checked deploy history for edge-proxy-3 — there was a config patch rolled at 02:10 that updated `/etc/nginx/sites-enabled/default` to reference `ssl_certificate /etc/ssl/certs/leaf.crt;` instead of `ssl_certificate /etc/ssl/certs/fullchain.pem;` (diff in config repo commit 6b7f3). The change was intended for a test path but accidentally deployed to prod bundle on proxy-3. Nginx was reloaded at 02:11 and not restarted afterwards.

ryan: quick repro locally: if `ssl_certificate` points at leaf-only file, `openssl s_client -showcerts` will only receive the leaf. confirmed.

maria: that matches symptoms (intermittent by IP). fix plan: replace `ssl_certificate` to fullchain, reload nginx on edge-proxy-3, verify openssl shows chain, and then confirm with customer. Doing now.

ryan: patched config, reloaded nginx on edge-proxy-3 at 02:46 UTC. Verified `openssl s_client -connect 10.10.4.23:443 -showcerts` now shows leaf+intermediate chain.

acme-sre: confirmed from our side — all IPs now return full chain and client errors have dropped to 0. Thanks! :tada:

maria: root cause summary (short): accidental config change on edge-proxy-3 replaced fullchain path with leaf-only path during deploy; rotator had uploaded correct bundle. Impact: intermittent TLS failures for requests routed to the misconfigured proxy. Remediation: config rollback + nginx reload.

alex: follow-ups: 1) add a pre-deploy NGINX config linter to catch fullchain vs leaf misrefs, 2) add a post-rotation probe that checks `openssl s_client -showcerts` against all edge IPs and alerts if any return incomplete chain, 3) consider tagging edge-proxies with canary flags so config patches don't hit singletons.

acme-sre: appreciated — those follow-ups would prevent this class of issue. We'll keep an eye and re-open if anything reappears.

ryan: adding retrospective note to deployment runbook and creating a small monitor: `probe/tls_chain_check` that asserts fullchain on all known endpoints.

maria: marking resolved. :white_check_mark:
